## Natural history notes

A small, dark skipper butterfly characterized by brown wings, pale translucent spots, and a broad-headed body with hooked antennae typical of skippers. In Florida, it is found in open woodlands, forest edges, scrub, pine flatwoods, roadsides, and other sunny habitats where legumes and nectar plants occur. Adults feed on nectar from low flowers and often perch with wings partly spread, while the caterpillars feed on plants in the pea family, using folded or tied leaves as shelters during development.
